design.title: Fly the average, not the last step: the exported model is the uniform average of the weights visited over the second half of training (SWAD/SWA-style dense weight averaging), with BatchNorm statistics recalibrated for the averaged weights
design.init_strategy: pretrained:efficientnet_b0 IMAGENET1K_V1 features[0..7] (torchvision, Apache-2.0 weights), fine-tuned at 0.1x LR — unchanged from experiment 19
design.eli5: Training a model is like a hiker wandering downhill in fog: where they happen to be standing at the moment we stop is a bit random, and often on a narrow ledge where a small change in the ground (a new photograph of the city) sends them tumbling. Instead of keeping the hiker's last footprint, we average all the spots they stood on during the second half of the walk. That average lands in the middle of a broad, flat valley, so a photograph taken in a different year, season or light moves the model's answer less. The drone carries exactly the same size of model; only the choice of which version we ship has changed.
design.hypothesis: Every architectural lever this era pulled has been the trunk, and the size gate now closes that road: experiment 19's export is 31.7 MB against a 32 MiB (33.6 MB) fp32 ceiling, so a bigger or third trunk cannot be added. What remains on the held-out truedop_2024 photograph is 6.5% abstention and 1.0% false fixes (usable 92.5%, mission 0.085), while the three training photographs read 100% usable / 0% false at the same held-out viewpoints: the residual is entirely the survey gap. A never-seen photograph is a shift of the input distribution, and the domain-generalisation literature is consistent on what a training procedure can do about such a shift with no extra capacity: the solution found by SGD's last iterate sits in a sharp region whose loss rises quickly under shift, while the average of the weights visited along the late trajectory sits in a flatter, wider minimum whose test loss rises much more slowly (SWA, Izmailov et al. UAI 2018; SWAD, Cha et al. NeurIPS 2021, which made dense weight averaging the strongest single domain-generalisation method on DomainBed, consistently beating ERM by 1.5-3 points out-of-domain, with gains concentrated in the shifted domains rather than the in-domain ones). That is exactly our split: in-domain is saturated (100%), out-of-domain is 92.5%. Nothing in 19 experiments of this era, nor any of the 83 earlier ones (searched: no EMA/SWA/weight-averaging row in lineage_history), has changed WHICH point of the trajectory is flown; every export is the last iterate of an 8-epoch run whose loss was still falling (6.16 -> 5.40 over epochs 5-8) and whose learning rate never drops below 0.1x, so the last iterate is still being kicked around by single-batch noise. Averaging is also the natural partner of the committee gate: frames abstain when one member's belief on the consensus block falls below 0.3, and a flatter member's softmax moves less when the photograph changes, so frames currently lost to one member wobbling should convert to usable fixes. Builds on experiment 19 (the champion) unchanged in architecture.
